milestones.title: An internet shared by the hour
milestones.body: A contemporary IDB account describes Peru's cabinas públicas: shared computers rented by the hour, with instruction and email services. The model offered a route online for people without their own computer or telephone line.
milestones.note: The starting year matches the author's birth year. It is not the year the internet began in Peru.

milestones.title: Broadband begins to grow
milestones.body: Telefónica del Perú reported 20,800 Speedy accesses in 2002, compared with 1,875 in 2001. Its annual report described Speedy as a high-speed internet service with a flat rate.
milestones.note: These are one operator's service accesses, not the number of internet users in Peru.

milestones.title: Cabinas reach more households
milestones.body: For October–December 2006, INEI findings relayed by OSIPTEL indicated that 61.2% of Lima households had at least one member who used a public internet cabina, compared with 40.7% a year earlier.
milestones.note: This measures household participation in Lima, not national home internet subscriptions.

milestones.title: A national broadband ambition
milestones.body: Published on 20 July 2012, Law 29904 promoted broadband and the construction of Peru's National Fibre Optic Backbone. The law gave a formal framework to the country's backbone project.
milestones.note: A policy milestone; publication of the law did not itself connect every household.

milestones.title: Spectrum for the 4G transition
milestones.body: In July 2013, Peru awarded two spectrum blocks in the 1.7/2.1 GHz band for mobile broadband. Telefónica's 2013 report separately lists 4G pre-sales, with service scheduled to operate from 2 January 2014.
milestones.note: The spectrum award and commercial service are different milestones. See the linked MTC record and the Telefónica 2013 source.

milestones.title: Fibre crosses the country
milestones.body: The Ministry of Transport and Communications records completion of the National Fibre Optic Backbone's deployment phase in September 2016. The project involved approximately 13,500 kilometres of fibre and entered its carrier-service phase.
milestones.note: A backbone transports communications between networks; it does not directly represent household connections.

milestones.title: A rural network opens in Moya
milestones.body: Internet para Todos launched its first connection platform in Moya, Huancavelica, on 28 June 2019. The partnership brought together Telefónica, Facebook, IDB Invest and CAF to expand rural mobile broadband infrastructure.
milestones.note: This is a documented local launch, not a claim that rural Peru was fully connected.

milestones.title: Lockdown changes network demand
milestones.body: OSIPTEL reported that data traffic during 16–20 March 2020 rose by 9–21% on mobile networks and 30–36% on fixed networks compared with the previous week, as Peru entered quarantine.
milestones.note: These short-term traffic increases measure network use, not the share of people connected.

milestones.title: Fibre leads fixed internet
milestones.body: At the end of 2024, OSIPTEL counted 4,069,739 fixed internet connections in Peru. Fibre accounted for 73.84% of that market, making it the most-used technology for fixed internet connections.
milestones.note: Connections include residential and business services; one connection can serve several people.

milestones.title: Progress remains uneven
milestones.body: INEI's fourth-quarter 2025 survey estimated internet service in 60.1% of Peru's households. The same measure was 78.2% in metropolitan Lima and 23.4% in rural areas: a gap of 54.8 percentage points.
milestones.note: Preliminary ENAHO estimates, published in March 2026. This is household access, not individual internet use.
